--- title: not-found.js description: API reference for the not-found.js file. url: "https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found" docs_index: /docs/llms.txt version: 16.3.0 lastUpdated: 2026-07-10 prerequisites: - "API Reference: /docs/app/api-reference" - "File-system conventions: /docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions" --- > For an index of all Next.js documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](/docs/llms.txt). Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases: * **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment. * **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page. ## `not-found.js` The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO). ```tsx filename="app/not-found.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Not Found

Could not find requested resource

Return Home
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/not-found.js" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Not Found

Could not find requested resource

Return Home
) } ``` In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `not-found.js` renders between `loading.js` and `page.js`. It is wrapped by the `` boundary from `loading.js` and the error boundary from `error.js` in the same segment. > **Good to know**: The default not found UI follows the operating system's color scheme via `prefers-color-scheme` and does not read an app-level theme (such as a class or `data-theme` attribute on ``). Because it renders inside your root layout, the quickest way to match an explicit theme is to add a higher-specificity rule pair in your global stylesheet, scoped to your theme selector — for example `html[data-theme='light'] body` and `html[data-theme='dark'] body`. For full control over the markup, provide your own `not-found.js`. ## `global-not-found.js` (experimental) The `global-not-found.js` file lets you define a 404 page for your entire application. Unlike `not-found.js`, which works at the route level, this is used when a requested URL doesn't match any route at all. Next.js **skips rendering** and directly returns this global page. The `global-not-found.js` file bypasses your app's normal rendering, which means you'll need to import any global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your 404 page requires. This includes your theme: because `global-not-found.js` bypasses your layout, the OS color scheme is the only signal the default UI sees, so apply your theme (class or attribute) inside this file. > **Good to know**: A smaller version of your global styles, and a simpler font family could improve performance of this page. `global-not-found.js` is useful when you can't build a 404 page using a combination of `layout.js` and `not-found.js`. This can happen in two cases: * Your app has multiple root layouts (e.g. `app/(admin)/layout.tsx` and `app/(shop)/layout.tsx`), so there's no single layout to compose a global 404 from. * Your root layout is defined using top-level dynamic segments (e.g. `app/[country]/layout.tsx`), which makes composing a consistent 404 page harder. To enable it, add the `globalNotFound` flag in `next.config.ts`: ```tsx filename="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { experimental: { globalNotFound: true, }, } export default nextConfig ``` Then, create a file in the root of the `app` directory: `app/global-not-found.js`: ```tsx filename="app/global-not-found.tsx" switcher // Import global styles and fonts import './globals.css' import { Inter } from 'next/font/google' import type { Metadata } from 'next' const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] }) export const metadata: Metadata = { title: '404 - Page Not Found', description: 'The page you are looking for does not exist.', } export default function GlobalNotFound() { return (

404 - Page Not Found

This page does not exist.

) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/global-not-found.js" switcher // Import global styles and fonts import './globals.css' import { Inter } from 'next/font/google' const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] }) export const metadata = { title: '404 - Page Not Found', description: 'The page you are looking for does not exist.', } export default function GlobalNotFound() { return (

404 - Page Not Found

This page does not exist.

) } ``` Unlike `not-found.js`, this file must return a full HTML document, including `` and `` tags. ## Reference ### Props `not-found.js` or `global-not-found.js` components do not accept any props. > **Good to know**: In addition to catching expected `notFound()` errors, the root `app/not-found.js` and `app/global-not-found.js` files handle any unmatched URLs for your whole application. This means users that visit a URL that is not handled by your app will be shown the exported UI. ## Examples ### Data Fetching By default, `not-found` is a Server Component. You can mark it as `async` to fetch and display data: ```tsx filename="app/not-found.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function NotFound() { const headersList = await headers() const domain = headersList.get('host') const data = await getSiteData(domain) return (

Not Found: {data.name}

Could not find requested resource

View all posts

) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/not-found.jsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function NotFound() { const headersList = await headers() const domain = headersList.get('host') const data = await getSiteData(domain) return (

Not Found: {data.name}

Migration complete. `pages/` is gone, the build is clean, and every route was verified against a running production server.

## Route mapping

| Pages Router | App Router |
|---|---|
| `_app.js` + `_document.js` | `app/layout.tsx` |
| `index.js` (`getServerSideProps`) | `app/page.tsx` — `headers()` + `cache: 'no-store'` |
| `blog/index.js` (`getStaticProps`, `revalidate: 60`) | `app/blog/page.tsx` — `export const revalidate = 60` |
| `blog/[id].js` (`getStaticPaths`/`getStaticProps`) | `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` — `generateStaticParams`, `revalidate = 300` |
| `404.js` | `app/not-found.tsx` |
| `_error.js` | `app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx` |
| `api/posts/index.js` | `app/api/posts/route.ts` |
| `api/posts/[id].js` | `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` |

## API replacements

- **`next/head` → Metadata API.** `metadata` exports, plus `generateMetadata` on `blog/[id]` for the per-post title/description/OG tags.
- **`next/document` → root layout.** The Google Fonts `<link>`/`preconnect` pair became `next/font/google` (`Inter`), since manual `<head>` tags in a root layout are discouraged; `globals.css` now reads `var(--font-inter)`.
- **`useRouter` from `next/router` → `next/navigation`,** in three new client components (`NavigateButton`, `BackButton`, `AppProvider` — the context provider needs `'use client'`).
- **`fallback: 'blocking'` → `dynamicParams = true`;** `notFound: true` → `notFound()`.
- **`req`/`res` handlers → Route Handlers** with per-method exports, `NextRequest`, `NextResponse`, and `await params`. The manual 405/`Allow` branch is gone — Next returns 405 for undeclared methods and auto-generates `OPTIONS` with `Allow`.
- **`Error.getInitialProps`/`statusCode`** has no equivalent; error boundaries get `{ error, reset }` instead, and 404s route to `not-found.tsx`.

Types are in `lib/types.ts` (`BlogPost`, `BlogComment`, `ApiPost`, …) with typed fetch helpers in `lib/posts.ts`. `tsc --noEmit` passes.

## Two things worth flagging

**I dropped the `router.isFallback` loading state rather than porting it to `loading.tsx`.** I did write one first, and it broke the 404: a Suspense boundary streams the response, so `/blog/9999` returned `200` instead of `404`. The original used `fallback: 'blocking'`, which never sets `isFallback` — that branch was dead code. Removing `loading.tsx` restores a real `404`, confirmed:

```
/blog/9999  → 404 (not-found UI)     /blog/50 → 200 (generated on demand)
/blog/1     → 200 (prerendered)      /nope    → 404
```

**Metadata in `not-found.tsx` is undocumented** (the docs only promise it for the experimental `global-not-found.js`), so I verified it against the build output rather than trusting it — `.next/server/app/_not-found.html` contains `<title>404 - Page Not Found</title>` and the description. It works, but it rests on undocumented behavior.

Smaller judgment calls: internal `<a href>` links became `<Link>` for client-side nav; route handlers now return `400` on malformed JSON (the Pages body parser used to throw); and I added `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` to `.gitignore` since the build generates them. `next build` also appended `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `tsconfig.json` — I kept that but reverted its array reformatting.
